newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee prices rise, but volume thin.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee prices rise, but volume thin.

text.p: Vietnamese coffee prices followed the New York and London markets higher over the week but trade ahead of the new 1996/97 season was thin, traders said on Friday.
They said robusta had been trading at around $1290 per tonne FOB Saigon Port compared with $1230 a week earlier.
"Volume has been very thin. There's not a great deal of interest right now," said one dealer.
Vietnam's coffee season lasts from October to September and output from the new harvest is expected to begin within a few weeks.
One trader said prospects for the new crop looked good because of relatively favourable weather conditions, the expansion of coffee growing areas and improved husbandry.
Separately, Doan Trieu Nhan, the head of the Vietnam Coffee Association, told Reuters on Friday that Vietnam had no plans at present to join the Association of Coffee Producing Countries.
He added that Hanoi had sent documents to the United Nations ratifying an International Coffee Organisation administrative pact. Further details were not available.
